disclaimer: Roku stream support varies by OS version, model, and chipset. These tables are conservative, doc-sourced hints, not absolute guarantees. The authoritative answer for any given device is the Video node's own errorInfo after a real playback attempt.

videoLimits.note: Roku H.264/AVC decoders top out at 1080p (level ~4.2). 4K/UHD requires HEVC, VP9, or AV1 — not H.264. H.264 above level 4.2 or above 1920x1080 is rejected on-device with errorCode -5, even though browsers/VLC decode it in software.

removedSystems.name: Verimatrix
removedSystems.note: Support for Verimatrix DRM was removed from the firmware in Roku OS 9.3. Re-protect content with Widevine or PlayReady.

drm.encryptionNote: In 2020+ the industry default is a single CMAF packaging encrypted with cbcs, signaled for both HLS and DASH. cenc-only content can play on Roku via Widevine/PlayReady but cannot be shared with FairPlay; cbcs is the safer cross-platform default.
drm.psshNote: For best video-start performance on DASH, the manifest should declare the DRM system and include a cenc:pssh box.
drm.libProviderNote: A 'BS lib provider not found' error means the DRM library is not installed. Installing a production app that uses that DRM loads the missing library (e.g. install YouTube to load Widevine, Netflix to load PlayReady).

segments.note: Segments should start with an IDR frame and be aligned across variants/representations. These properties cannot be verified from the manifest alone.

errorCodes.-1: network error (server down/unreachable, or a client network setup problem)
errorCodes.-4: empty list — no streams were specified to play
errorCodes.-5: media error — the media format is unknown or unsupported

errorCategories.http: Networking/HTTP layer (download failures, bad status, redirects, timeouts).
errorCategories.drm: DRM layer (license acquisition, key handling, DRM lib).
